name: Venezia
lede: Venezia is the Italian name of Venice, used for a deep greenish blue in a 1930 American color dictionary; the books say nothing about it as a color.

sections.title: A name with no recorded story
sections.body:
The color comes from Maerz and Paul's 1930 *Dictionary of Color*, which places it on plate 36, block K6, and gives 1927 as its first recorded use [1]. Who named it, and why, is undocumented. The books in our collection only match the word in bibliography titles about Italian dyeing, and none describes this color [2]. It was listed under fashion and textiles in our data, which fits a 1920s name [1].

On screen it is close to [[petrol]], 7.9 units away, and to [[teal-blue]] [1]. A cleaner relative is [[teal]], and a deeper one [[blue]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 museum paintings, 36 contain a color within six units of this one over at least five per cent of the canvas [3]. Most are 1800s works, 14 of the 36, and seven are American [3]. The set includes Van Gogh's 1889 *Self-Portrait* and, fittingly, Monet's *Palazzo da Mula, Venice* of 1908 [3]. The photographs show aged, varnished paintings, so this is a color match, not a claim about pigment [3].
